test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following best explains the origin of eskers in glaciated landscapes?

options.text: Ridges carved by ice cutting bedrock
Sinuous ridges from subglacial meltwater deposition
Hills shaped by ice pushing sediments

solution:
The correct answer is __**Sinuous ridges from subglacial meltwater deposition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Eskers** are described as long, narrow, **sinuous ridges** composed of **stratified sand and gravel**. They are primary landforms resulting from **glacio-fluvial deposition**.
 
• The formation occurs when **meltwater** flows through **tunnels** within or beneath a **stagnant glacier**. As the glacier melts away, the sediment that settled on the floor of these tunnels is left behind as a winding ridge. ***Hence, the statement regarding subglacial meltwater deposition is correct.***
 
• Unlike **glacial till**, which is unsorted, the materials in an esker are **sorted and stratified** because they were transported and deposited by **running water**.
 
• These ridges typically run parallel to the direction of **ice flow**. They can reach heights of **10 to 50 meters** and extend for **hundreds of kilometers** in some regions, such as those found in **Canada**
